description: Juliana stops midway down the aisle, confronted by a haughty matriarch stepping into the foreground.
Lady in Gold Gown: 'Because he is marrying me.' Juliana gasps in shock.
Gerald: 'I changed my mind.' Juliana: 'You swore you loved me!'
Lady in Gold Gown: 'You are the daughter people tolerate because they have to.' Juliana absorbs the venomous words.
Gerald coldly rejects Juliana, calling her plain, silent, and beneath him while Clarissa smiles.
Juliana delivers a scathing indictment of Gerald's honor, declaring she will not be ashamed.
The Noble Matriarch coldly tells Juliana she has humiliated the family enough and must leave.
The Bearded Stranger confronts the Noble Matriarch, demanding she let go of Juliana.
The Bearded Stranger drops a royal guard with a single punch, shocking Gerald and the congregation.
The Bearded Stranger pulls a silver ring from his pocket and offers it to Juliana.
Gerald mocks Juliana for accepting a ring from a penniless stranger, while Clarissa laughs.
The stranger looks past Gerald and declares Juliana is a woman betrayed, not a woman who deserves to be discarded.
The Priest begins to pronounce them husband and wife as the stranger rises to his feet.
The Priest raises his hands to pronounce them husband and wife.
Lord Ashcroft declares Juliana is dead to the family and revokes her dowry and inheritance.
Lady Ashcroft snatches Juliana's mother's ledger and violently flings it into the mud.
Juliana drops to her knees in the mud, reaching for her fallen mother's book.
The Mysterious Bearded Man threatens Gerald: 'Choose your next words carefully.'
Juliana and the Mysterious Bearded Man arrive at the cottage, and she asks, 'That is it?'
Juliana marches toward the cottage door, declaring, 'At least no one there will be waiting to humiliate me.'
The Mysterious Bearded Man stands in the dim light and apologizes, 'I am sorry.'
Juliana meets his gaze and says, 'I am.'
Juliana lifts her chin and declares she remains a lady despite her soiled hands.
Juliana dismisses Gerald with utter contempt, commanding him to leave.
The Scarred Bearded Man towers menacingly over Gerald, freezing him with fear.
The husband looks down at Juliana with quiet affection after saving her.
Alexander, bathed in warm hearth embers, offers a subtle, knowing half-smile.
Alexander firmly catches Juliana's wrist in midair, his gaze locked onto hers.
Alexander points to a botanical illustration, explaining how crushed leaves ease swelling.
Juliana looks across at Alexander's battle-marked features with empathy, asking if his scars were from the war.
Frantic pounding on the door interrupts Juliana's work. A soaked peasant mother begs for help, claiming her child is burning with fever.
Juliana reads from her mother's grimoire, identifying 'Feverfew' and 'Chamomile' as the cure.
The fever breaks and the mother looks up at Juliana with overwhelming gratitude, whispering, 'You saved him.'
The Former Groom reveals that the rumored man has the same scar the Duke carried after the war.
Alexander bursts into the cottage, panting heavily and clutching his bloodied coat.
Alexander reveals his muscular torso crisscrossed with jagged battle scars.
Juliana tells Alexander, 'You have suffered terribly,' and he replies, 'It is over.'
Alexander confesses to Juliana, 'Your touch is the only medicine that has ever eased my pain.'
Gerald accuses Alexander of stealing his gold pocket watch, and Juliana gasps in disbelief.
Gerald mocks Alexander as a beggar, and Alexander steps past Juliana with a murderous gaze.
Gerald taunts Alexander to let the Constable search, and Alexander coldly agrees, 'Search it.'
The Constable pulls a gold pocket watch from Alexander's coat, and Juliana gasps in horror.
Clarissa mocks Juliana for defending her 'broken scrap of a man,' and Juliana counters with a steely, resolute question.
Clarissa describes her emerald signet ring lost in frozen, razor-sharp blackthorn briars, setting up a dangerous task.
Clarissa whispers that Juliana will watch her husband hang if she fails to retrieve the ring.
Juliana declares she will not let them take Alexander and demands to know where the garden is.
Clarissa and Gerald stand on the balcony, mocking Juliana as she prepares to crawl into the frozen blackthorn garden.
Juliana's bare hands are raked by blackthorn spines, carving bloody gashes across her skin as Clarissa gleefully points down.
Juliana screams in agony as her hand gets snagged between two vicious thorns, tearing her flesh and sleeve.
Juliana's blood-smeared finger brushes against a massive, radiant emerald signet ring buried in the frozen soil.
Alexander tenderly examines Juliana's bleeding, lacerated hands, asking what they have done to her.
Alexander carries Juliana bridal-style, whispering that she should never have had to bleed for him.
Alexander kisses Juliana's head and vows that no one will ever hurt her for protecting him again.
Alexander clenches his fist into an iron ball of vengeance as the screen cuts to black.
A thug smashes a wooden planter box, shattering the frame with a loud crash.
The bald thug grinds his boot into the crushed flowers while Juliana watches in horror.
Juliana crawls through the mud, fresh blood seeping through her bandaged hands.
The Tall Thug hoists his club to crush the remaining herbs right before Juliana.
Alexander catches a thug's iron pipe mid-air with his bare hand.
The Bald Thug charges in, shouting, 'Aaargh!' as Alexander hurls him.
The Thug with Cap screams, 'Gerald Harrington paid us!' and Juliana gasps.
Alexander turns away, haunted by his past as Juliana looks on.
Alexander kneels before Juliana and vows no one will hurt her again.
Juliana confesses she is frightened of losing Alexander, and he pulls her into a hug.
Juliana playfully teases Alexander about his long hair, and he smirks.
Juliana reflects on not knowing the man she married, and the scene fades out.
A violent crash as the bedroom door is kicked open and Alexander bursts in, looking like an imposing guardian amid the blaze.
Juliana spots her mother's herbal ledger and halts, pointing back toward the burning desk as Alexander shouts, 'Leave it!'
Alexander leaps through the burning window frame, carrying Juliana safely out into the night as the parlor collapses behind them.
Alexander's expression hardens into a mask of pure, lethal fury as he vows, 'They took our home. I will not let them take anything else now.'
Alexander accepts blankets and bread from a villager, and Juliana says goodbye to the ruins of Blackwood cottage.
The bald informant bows to Alexander, revealing he is an operative reporting on Lord Sterling's takeover.
Alexander clenches his fist in rage as the informant reveals that his mother is a prisoner in her own house.
Juliana breaks down in tears in the barn, and Alexander comforts her by wrapping a blanket around her.
Rupert and Catherine discuss the Dowager Duchess's slow death, with Rupert gloating that he has ensured her quiet comfort through the winter.
Juliana refuses to stop working in the freezing barn to save the village, telling Seamus, 'If I stop, the lung fever in the valley wins.'
Juliana stands up to Seamus's grief, declaring, 'They have reduced me to myself. And I am not finished.'
Catherine dismisses the villagers' suffering, telling Rupert, 'Let the peasants rot in their barns. Let them pray to their weeds.'
Prudence drops to her knees on the hay-strewn barn floor, pleading for Juliana to save her dying brother Toby.
Juliana commands Prudence to fetch hot water immediately, and Prudence rushes to obey.
Juliana directs the medicinal steam toward Toby's face, whispering, 'Lift his shoulders, Prudence. Hold the steam close.'
Juliana turns sharply with sudden recognition and asks Prudence, 'What do you mean? Is someone ill? The Dowager Duchess?'
Juliana swallows her pride and accepts her perilous disguise, stating, 'Today, I am only a maid.'
Prudence introduces Juliana to the Housekeeper as 'Julian, ma'am. New help for the winter cleaning.'
Juliana twists the latch handle of the ornate door, and the camera pushes into the shadowy bedchamber.
Juliana realizes the Duchess's illness is unnatural and asks, 'Who has been treating you?'
Close-up of the Duchess's fingertips revealing pronounced dark, purplish-black discoloration beneath the nails.
Lady Juliana stands upright, her expression hardening with fierce skepticism, and pulls out a worn, leather-bound notebook.
Lady Juliana declares 'Arsenic' as the Duchess chokes and spasms on the bed.
The door latch turns and the heavy door cracks open inward.
The noblewoman strikes Juliana with a riding crop and coldly states she is just a maid.
The noblewoman drags Juliana and Prudence into a dark room and commands her to clean the hearth.
Juliana pauses scrubbing to touch the hidden remedy book and vows to return.
Alexander pulls back the torn fabric of Juliana's cloak to reveal a raw, bloody welt on her shoulder.
Juliana whispers the name of her attacker, 'Lady Catherine,' as Alexander stares at her intensely.
Juliana reveals the horrifying truth that the Dowager Duchess is being poisoned with arsenic.
Alexander trembles with terrified passion, warning, 'This time,' as Juliana insists she is being careful.
Juliana whispers that if the guards hear them, they are both dead, and the Duchess clutches the blanket in dismay.
The Duchess asks why a girl of noble spirit works as a common maid, and Juliana admits her family cast her out to rot.
Juliana rests her hand against the bedcover, revealing a distinctive engraved signet ring, and the Duchess gasps in shock.
The Duchess clamps Juliana's hand, demanding to know where she got the ring.
The Dowager Duchess grips Juliana's forearm with fierce insistence, crying, "My lost son wore that ring!"
The Blond Nobleman steps forward and commands, "Girl. Show me what you are holding."
Juliana raises the bottle and declares, "It is an antidote." Lady Catherine sneers, "An antidote to what?"
Juliana states the grim reality, "Poison." The Blond Nobleman's expression freezes into a dark scowl.
The Dowager Duchess stirs and commands Rupert to stop, insisting Juliana is innocent and saved her.
Catherine ruthlessly yanks the silver locket off Juliana's neck, causing her to scream in agony.
Catherine reads the handwritten inscription 'Juliana Ashcroft' from the herbarium, revealing her secret identity.
Juliana reaches frantically for her mother's book as Catherine threatens to hang her before the magistrate.
Catherine disdainfully describes the herbarium's contents as 'roots. leaves. powders' and calls it witchcraft, while Juliana lunges in outrage.
Catherine whispers she will burn the book and that no one will remember what was written inside.
The guards shove Juliana violently onto the wet floor and slam the heavy iron door shut.
Juliana vows she will not let them take Alexander, and the portcullis bars drop.
The Elder Nobleman aggressively pins Rupert against the wall with his cane and commands, 'We stop hiding the prisoner.'
Catherine asks if Juliana will claim to be a healer, and the Elder Nobleman coldly replies, 'Then call it witchcraft.'
Catherine mentions Juliana's 'botanical ledger' as the key evidence to be used against her.
Catherine exults that Juliana will hang and the town will cheer, while the Elder Nobleman declares she becomes a witch.
Juliana declares she became a disgrace when she refused to become cruel.
Juliana looks up and says she calls it love.
Juliana reaches for her mother's book but is restrained by chains.
The red-hot iron stops inches from Juliana's face.
Catherine is confused when Juliana defiantly commands, 'Burn the ledger.'
Catherine screams, 'You are lying!' and brandishes the glowing tong in Juliana's face.
Juliana declares, 'My husband,' and Catherine responds, 'He is a nobody.'
Catherine plunges the glowing iron toward Juliana's face, stopping inches from her eye.
The maid defends Juliana, claiming she watched her save the boy.
The Lord asks if Juliana used a forbidden book and the maid admits it.
The maid begs for her brother's life, revealing he is only seven years old.
The maid collapses in despair, and the Lord coldly dismisses her tears.
Judge commands Prudence to testify, and the terrified young maid stands trembling in the center of the courtroom.
Lady Juliana slams her cuffed hands against the wooden railing of the dock, her voice ringing out in indignant fury.
Lady Juliana directly admits to administering the herbal mixtures, explaining there was no physician willing to help.
Lady Juliana unflinchingly refuses to renounce her practices, and the Judge lowers his brow with dark finality.
Alexander's mother drops her staff and rushes to embrace her presumed-dead son.
Alexander's mother tearfully confesses, 'I buried you,' and he replies, 'I know.'
Alexander reveals he was shot and left for dead, crawling away from the battlefield.
Alexander identifies the traitors as the men currently ruling Ashwood, leaving his mother horrified.
Alexander (Spitting with Contempt): 'They wanted the investigation buried.'
Alexander's Mother (Wailing): 'They arrested her!' Alexander's Mother (Despairing): 'Rupert and Catherine accused her of poisoning me!'
Alexander's Mother (Solemn, Shattered): 'She is to be executed.' Alexander's Mother (Trembling): 'After the wedding.'
Alexander (Cold, Thunderous Finale): '...their dead Duke is coming home.'
Rupert and Catherine plot their wedding and the public execution of Juliana.
Clarissa reads the invitation and reveals the sentencing of the condemned.
Juliana refuses to eat the food in her dungeon cell.
Juliana grips the iron ring in the dungeon pillar, vowing to keep her identity.
A compassionate guard whispers to a starving Juliana that no one should die hungry before slipping her bread through the bars.
Starving and overcome with emotion, Juliana presses the bread to her lips and tears off a desperate, ravenous bite.
Juliana vows, 'I will not give them my husband,' and declares she will not betray him, her eyes flashing with fierce loyalty.
Juliana realizes the wedding bells are tolling and grimly concludes, 'Then I suppose I'm next,' as she stares down the corridor.
The cart driver lunges at a royal sentry, tackling him violently against the carriage wheel.
The loyalist fighter whispers, 'Sleep,' as the sentry goes limp in his sleeper hold.
Alexander stares at his rugged reflection in a cracked mirror, tracing a scar.
A loyalist soldier drops to his knee before Alexander, calling him 'Your Grace.'
Lady Harrington taunts Lord Harrington about Juliana seeing the wedding, and he coldly replies she won't see anything for long.
An elder nobleman demands the entrances to the cathedral are covered, and the Royal Guard confirms they are sealed.
Lady Harrington whispers in awe that Catherine looks like a queen, while Rupert takes her hands at the altar.
The elder nobleman vows the 'witch' will be dead by sunset, as the cathedral doors open and light floods the nave.
A noblewoman whispers that Juliana has returned to the chapel, but not as a bride.
Extreme close-up of Juliana's scarred, dirtied wrists bound tight in heavy iron shackles.
The cathedral entrance explodes, sending debris and terrified screams through the congregation.
Silhouetted armed figures emerge through the smoke and rubble, and Juliana turns her head toward the light.
Royal Guard refuses to arrest Alexander, declaring he knows who the Duke is.
Rupert denies Alexander's identity, claiming he died, while Alexander counters that he stands before them.
Alexander's mother gently cradles his scarred cheek, weeping with joy.
Alexander threatens Rupert with his sword, vowing to settle the score.
Royal Guard Captain refuses Rupert's order and points his sword at him.
Alexander reveals a War Office dossier stamped 'TOP SECRET'.
Alexander steps forward and demands the Crown Official read the names.
Police Constable blocks Lord Sterling's escape at the cathedral door.
Catherine weeps and trembles, confessing that she waited three years believing Alexander was dead.
Alexander abruptly pulls his face away from Catherine's touch, leaving her hand suspended in mid-air.
Alexander delivers the cold line, 'You were never my Duchess,' as Catherine breaks down in tears.
The camera tilts up from the floor to reveal Juliana's shackled wrists, showing the true bride waiting.
Juliana gasps in awe as Alexander reveals his identity as the Duke
Alexander accuses Catherine of poisoning his mother as she gasps in denial
Alexander proclaims Juliana Duchess of Ashburton as Rupert stares in horror
Catherine's despair morphs into a triumphant smirk as the episode ends
The High Priest declares their marriage invalid as Alexander turns to protect Juliana.
The High Priest says 'Love doesn't make a Duchess, girl. Paper does.'
Juliana shouts at the priest that God married them, not him.
The High Priest threatens that if they lose the trial, the county will watch them lose her twice.
Catherine grabs Agnes by the hands and declares that everyone in the chapel saw her humiliated.
Agnes nervously warns Catherine that the Duke has bailiffs watching every road out of the county.
Catherine places a heavy velvet coin purse into Agnes's hands and orders her to send for the priest tonight.
Agnes stashes the pouch into her apron and hurries out into the darkness.
Catherine warns Father Thomas that if anyone suspects his face, their alliance is over.
Catherine demands Father Thomas stall the council hearing and asks what she actually needs from him.
Father Thomas warns that if he conspires against the Duke, he will hang when the truth comes out.
Catherine promises Father Thomas that a grateful Duchess collects debts differently than a desperate one.
Catherine playfully teases Father Thomas about his stamina in his collar, while he retorts that a man in his collar shouldn't even be in the bed.
Father Thomas demands the west territory's tax collection routed through his office as the price for his silence.
Catherine and Father Thomas embrace passionately in the abandoned wing, lost in their forbidden entanglement.
Agnes peeks through the crack of the door and sees Catherine and the shirtless priest locked in an intimate embrace.
